ratings.comment: Camera-based food recognition directly enables put-food-in-and-press-start operation, though reliable portion and doneness inference remains technically challenging.
Combined weight and IR sensing with a single start button strongly serves the no-learning-curve need using plausible, relatively cheap components.

Switch-mode HV supply is mostly an invisible internal improvement and does little to make the microwave simpler for the user.
Fanless heat-pipe cooling could remove post-cycle fan confusion, but passively cooling a magnetron is thermally difficult and only tangentially related to simple operation.
Voice commands can reduce learning, but low-cost keyword spotting still limits commands and may mishear.

Three outcome pictures are immediately understandable, though preset buttons are already familiar.
Inverter drives improve power control but are established technology and still leave time-setting complexity.
